title: Multiprocessing vs Multithreading
prompt: Explain how multiprocessing differs from multithreading. When would you choose each? Give an example of how you used threads in a project and explain why they suited the work.

references.label: Canonical Notion question — xAI multiprocessing versus multithreading

response.placeholder: Compare the mechanisms, explain when you would choose each, then use a truthful project example.
response.reference_answer:
## Core distinction

Processes usually have separate address spaces and communicate explicitly. Threads share an address space, making data sharing inexpensive but requiring coordination for mutable state. Compare isolation, startup cost, memory use, and communication overhead.

## Choosing

For CPU-heavy work, ask whether the runtime permits parallel execution and measure communication overhead. In a conventional GIL-enabled CPython build, threads do not generally execute Python bytecode in parallel; native extensions and free-threaded builds change that boundary. Threads can overlap I/O waits, while processes can isolate independent work and failures. Neither choice removes the need to manage cancellation and shared external resources.

## Project example

Describe a project you actually worked on: what waited or ran in parallel, why threads fit, what state was shared, how you synchronized it, and what evidence showed an improvement. Do not present a hypothetical example as personal experience.

The role does not turn this CS fundamentals question into ML system design. The written response is a practice format; no implementation task was reported.
